newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish quiet afternoon lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish quiet afternoon lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended lower in quiet trade, unable to shrug off early weakness.

Debt futures initially upticked after May consumer price data, but profit-taking quickly hit the market. Not long after, strong May industrial production and capacity utilization data added fuel to the fire and debt futures touched session lows.
Trade was very quiet the rest of the day, traders said.
"The market in my mind closed down around 10:45," said Rick Santelli, vice president of futures and options for Rand Financial.
"We saw good trade right after the (CPI) number and a much better trade after the 8:15 numbers," Santelli said.
May CPI rose 0.1 percent and gained 0.2 percent excluding food and energy prices, versus average trade estimates for 0.2-percent increases in both rates.
At 0815 CDT/1315 GMT, May industrial output was reported up 0.4 percent and April's production was revised to up 0.3 percent. Capacity use gained to 83.7 from 83.6 in April.
September Treasury bond futures slipped to 111-17/32 in morning trade, but lethargy reigned the rest of the day, traders said. Support at 111-11/32 was untouched, they added.
Santelli said September's close above 111-25/32 likely means the market will consolidate, "but it's not a disaster."
Prices had no reaction late in the day to the Redbook Retail Sales Index, which showed U.S. adjusted retail sales up 1.7 percent.
"The market was long coming into today and I think the market just looked a little tired at these lofty levels," a Eurodollar trader said.
He said September and December Euros "have definitely taken a tightening out of the market," and possibly went too far on the upside.

At the close, September T-bonds were off 6/32 at 111-28/32, September 10-year notes fell 04/32 to 108-14/32, December T-bills were down 0.030 at 94.67, and December Eurodollars were off 0.02 at 93.95. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
